steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“PT” in late October means Pacific Time, which is still on daylight saving time then: **PDT (UTC−7)**.  
Madrid on **2026-10-30** is still on **CEST (UTC+2)**, since Spain’s DST ends later that weekend.

So Madrid is **9 hours ahead** of Pacific Time.

- Deadline given: **Friday, 2026-10-30 at 11:59 PM PT**
- Add 9 hours in Madrid:
  - **2026-10-31 08:59** in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“Today” is Friday, 2026-10-30, so “this coming Monday” is 2026-11-02.

Los Angeles on 2026-11-02 is on PST (UTC-8), because daylight saving time ends the day before, on Sunday, 2026-11-01.  
Madrid on 2026-11-02 is on CET (UTC+1), since Europe has already switched off daylight saving time the previous week.

So Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles at that moment.

10:00 AM in Los Angeles + 9 hours = 19:00 in Madrid, same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid, Spain is on local Madrid time, so no conversion is needed.

Start:
- Saturday, 2026-10-24 at 18:00 in Madrid

Add 48 hours:
- +24 hours = Sunday, 2026-10-25 at 18:00
- +24 more hours = Monday, 2026-10-26 at 18:00

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CET/CEST, and on **October 29, 2026** Madrid will be on **CET (UTC+1)** because daylight saving time in Spain ends the previous weekend.

“PT” in late October is **Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7)** until the U.S. switches in early November.

- Start: **2026-10-26 10:00 AM PT**
- Add 72 hours: **2026-10-29 10:00 AM PT**
- Convert from **UTC-7** to Madrid **UTC+1**: add **8 hours**

So the deadline in Madrid is **2026-10-29 18:00**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“ET” in late October is still Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC−4), because U.S. daylight saving time ends in early November.

- Submissions close: 2026-10-31 23:59 ET = 2026-11-01 03:59 UTC
- Add 36 hours: 2026-11-02 15:59 UTC

Madrid on 2026-11-02 is on CET (UTC+1), since Spain has already switched back from summer time the week before.

- 2026-11-02 15:59 UTC = 2026-11-02 16:59 in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Unix timestamp **1791788340** corresponds to **2026-10-12 03:39:00 UTC**.

Tokyo, Japan is **JST (UTC+9)** year-round, so add 9 hours:

**2026-10-12 12:39 JST**

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 12:39

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

`2026-10-25T02:30:00Z` is in UTC.

Madrid is on **CEST (UTC+2)** on **October 25, 2026** until the DST change later that morning, so you add 2 hours:

- 02:30 UTC
- = **04:30** in Madrid local time

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is **October 25, 2026**.

“Pacific Time” in late October is still **Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC−7)** because the U.S. hasn’t switched off daylight saving yet.  
Madrid, Spain at that date is on **CEST (UTC+2)** until the early hours of the next Sunday changeover.

So Madrid is **9 hours ahead** of Pacific Time.

- **11:59 PM PDT on 2026-10-25**
- plus **9 hours**
- = **8:59 AM on 2026-10-26** in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, the US ends daylight saving time on **Sunday, November 1, 2026**. After the change, **Eastern Time** is **EST (UTC−5)**.

Lima, Peru is **PET (UTC−5)** year-round, so at that point **Eastern Time and Lima time are the same**.

Therefore, **12:00 noon Eastern Time** is **12:00 noon in Lima** on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“AoE” means **Anywhere on Earth**, which is effectively **UTC−12**.  
So **December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE** = **January 1, 2027, 00:00 in UTC−12**.

Tokyo is **JST = UTC+9**, which is **21 hours ahead** of UTC−12.

Add 21 hours:
- 2027-01-01 00:00 (AoE)
- → **2027-01-01 21:00 JST**

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney on October 5, 2026 is in AEDT (UTC+11) because daylight saving time starts the day before. New York on October 5, 2026 is in EDT (UTC-4).

So New York is 15 hours behind Sydney.

5:00 PM in Sydney on 2026-10-05 minus 15 hours = 2:00 AM in New York on 2026-10-05.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
